name: World Championship
epitaph: EPW's World Championship was first won by Hudman, before 2003-08-24. The fed's own record carries 4 reigns on it, across 4 different champions. The longest is John Adams's, 189 days from 21 September 2003. Chapel held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: EPW's Intercontinental Championship was first won by Hudman, before 2003-08-15. The fed's own record carries 6 reigns on it, across 6 different champions. The longest is Chapel's, 168 days from 9 January 2004. Ace held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Hardcore Championship
epitaph: EPW's Hardcore Championship was first won by Blackheart on 1 August 2003. The fed's own record carries 3 reigns on it, across 3 different champions. The longest is King Hardkore's, 131 days from 24 August 2003. One of its reigns ended outside a match — vacated. The belt was vacated on an unrecorded date after Tom Conway's reign, and the surviving record carries no later change.

name: Tag Team Championship
epitaph: EPW's Tag Team Championship was first won by Blackheart and Mephisto on 24 August 2003. The fed's own record carries 4 reigns on it, across 4 different champions. The longest is Mike Stryker and Devildriver's, 24 days from 28 August 2003. One of its reigns ended outside a match — retired with the belt. EPW did away with it on 8 June 2004 until a tag team division could be established.

events.note: The fed's news post of 8 June 2004 says officials decided to do away with the gold until a tag team division could be established.

name: Legacy Championship
epitaph: EPW's Legacy Championship was first won by Tom Conway on 11 July 2004. Tom Conway held it at the end of the surviving record.
